Question
========
A team must choose between local servers and a cloud provider. The service must support 10 000 req/s. A local server handles 100 req/s, costs 3000 kg CO2e and draws 200 W. A cloud VM handles 50 req/s, is charged 300 kg CO2e, that is 1/10 of a server, and draws 150 W. Electricity is 170 g CO2e/kWh, devices are replaced every 5 years, horizon 5 years of 365 days. Ignore scope 1.

Compute the counts, the manufacturing emissions, the operational emissions, the totals, and say which is better.

Solution
========
Five years is 43800 hours.

Counts: local 10000/100 = 100 servers; cloud 10000/50 = 200 VMs.

Manufacturing: local 100 x 3000 = 300 000 kg; cloud 200 x 300 = 60 000 kg.

Electricity: local 100 x 200 = 20 000 W, so 876 000 kWh, times 170 g = 148 920 kg.
  Cloud 200 x 150 = 30 000 W, so 1 314 000 kWh, times 170 g = 223 380 kg.

Totals: local 448 920 kg; cloud 283 380 kg.

The cloud is better by about 1.6x, even though it burns 1.5 times more electricity, because the attributed manufacturing is five times smaller. As in the other variants of this question, the conclusion is driven by the 1/10 sharing hypothesis and by the fact that manufacturing dominates.
